title: P1: Customer balance capacity is O(ledger) per priced admission under a per-account lock

title: UX-27: Uncertain key creation or rotation is presented as safely retryable
description:
Source: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md (UX-27). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: New: uncertain key mutation lacks reconciliation and safe recovery

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · state/recovery · isolated frontend probes + backend source.** A network rejection leaves an error and re-enables Create/Rotate without checking saved state or warning that the operation may have committed. The backend issues/rotates before constructing the complete response. After response loss, a create retry can create a second credential; a successful rotation may have already invalidated the old secret while the user never received the new one. These consequences are inferred from the implementation path; they were not induced on real keys.

Criterion: distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed failure, prevent harmful retries, and offer a usable recovery path. An intentionally one-time secret is valid; pretending it can always be recovered is not a correction.

Proposed correction: reconcile operation outcome using a suitable request identity/status contract or an equally safe supported flow. Explain the uncertain credential state and direct the owner through explicit recovery. Preserve secret non-retrievability and prevent accidental duplicate issuance. Compare TopupFunding's existing uncertain-result handling rather than designing a generic retry loop.

Acceptance: test response loss both before and after commit, server error after commit, navigation/re-entry and role loss. No blind duplicate creation; rotation clearly communicates old-secret status and how to obtain usable replacement access. A confirmed validation failure remains directly correctable. Test frontend and backend together before accepting the repair.

**P1 · recovery/journey · live + source.** In the existing blocked-request list, an input or external-detector denial shows the key, time and policy version. Neither the reason nor policy is actionable. The only investigation action is generic Logs, although the page explains that these blocks precede dispatch and some admission denials are not recorded. Criterion: meaningful error diagnosis/recovery and recognition rather than recall. Do not disclose rejected prompt content merely to improve diagnosis.

Proposed correction: attach authorized historical policy/check evidence and a scope-preserving remedy, or explicitly state which evidence is unavailable and how to obtain help. Keep pre-dispatch events distinct from dispatched request logs.

Acceptance: from a recorded block, the appropriate role can inspect the policy version and available cause, identify who can remedy it, and return to the event. A changed/deleted detector is labelled historically or unavailable, not silently replaced by its current configuration. A reader does not receive editing rights.

title: UX-19: A section-local Save can commit hidden changes from another policy section
description:
Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-19). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Reproduced E07: hidden cross-section changes share a Save

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · consequential edit scope · G6, J7 · high confidence in draft behavior and save implementation; no policy submitted.**

In Model access, changing the unsaved model restriction to Block all enables Save. Navigating through Policy preserves the draft and shows a generic unsaved-changes notice, while the access card still says No restrictions from the saved policy. Opening External checks then shows an enabled Save despite no detector changes and no available detectors. That page provides no indication that a model restriction is pending. The shared `Guardrails` component submits the entire `draft` from every section's Save handler. Evidence: E30, actual unsaved navigation and screenshot, plus `features/guardrails/page.tsx` draft lifetime and PUT payload.

Impact: saving from an apparently unrelated section can also commit a hidden workspace-wide model block. The section title and local controls do not describe the effective submission scope. No actual block was enabled: Save was never clicked, and reloading cleared the test draft and disabled Save. The existence of one generic notice on the intermediate Policy page is mitigating evidence, but does not expose the pending changes at the commit point.

Proposed direction: make the commit boundary understandable. Either use explicitly section-scoped drafts and saves, or present a whole-policy editing model with a reviewable pending-change summary and discard path at its save point. Preserve atomic policy validation and revision conflict handling; do not assume separate API writes are required.

Verification: edit section A, visit B without editing it, and establish exactly which changes B's action would commit. Repeat with changes in both sections, invalid hidden input, cancellation, reload and conflict. Users can inspect and discard the affected changes before committing. Verify the saved outcome only with authorized isolated fixtures. [NN/g's usability heuristics](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/) support visible state, error prevention and recognition at the point of action; they do not mandate a confirmation dialog for every save.

An existing balance, credit allowance or personal upstream key is not an implicit exemption from this setup gate.

Required direction: establish one server-authoritative installation payment-readiness gate shared by all workspaces. Apply the gate consistently to direct URLs, existing sessions and workspace API operations, not only navigation visibility. Preserve existing data and allow already-started payment callbacks, reconciliation and request settlement to complete. This gate is distinct from each customer's balance and from a single failed or pending payment; those do not by themselves make the whole installation unconfigured.
